name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: Teams will let you pop out a sign language interpreter, Edge 158 puts workspaces in one window, Foundry previews Programmed Training, and a Cornell-LSU team wins a $200,000 quantum prize.
window: Window: the week's best, from the 80 hours to 06:38 AEDT, Sun 22 Nov 2026 (Wednesday 18 to Saturday 21 Nov in the US), plus This-week items.
notes: A thin week for new education-specific news: the week's education stories (Microsoft Classroom, Study and Learn in assignments, Hour of AI, Hwb) were covered 18-21 Nov. Cornell's Quantum Pioneers story (19 Nov) adapts an October LSU release. This week: the AI Transparency Initiative (announced 17 Nov; the education press covered it 19 Nov).

Coming, not shipped: the sign language interpreter pop-out (preview December, due January 2027), Teams meeting AI controls and Teams Rooms timers (due January 2027), Exchange HVE external sending (preview December, due March 2027) and the AI Interpreter (now due February 2027) are roadmap items in development; Programmed Training and multi-turn evaluation are in public preview; LE Audio stereo and the People widget are in the Experimental channel for Windows Insiders. Edge 158 reached Stable on 19 Nov.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 22 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
ON THE SAME PAGE. 🤝

stories.title: Teams will let you pop out a sign language interpreter's video
stories.summary: Roadmap item 571387, in development: in Teams on desktop and Mac you'll be able to pop out a sign language interpreter into a separate, resizable window that stays visible across monitors and apps while you share content or change layouts. It's designed to support Deaf and hard of hearing users.
stories.for: Deaf and hard-of-hearing students, staff and interpreters

stories.title: Teams meeting organizers will decide who can use Copilot and AI
stories.summary: Roadmap item 577399, in development: Teams meetings get enhanced Copilot and AI controls. Organizers manage who can enable and access AI in their meetings, and IT admins get a simpler policy model for governing AI across meetings and post-meeting experiences.
stories.for: Teachers who run class and parent meetings, and school IT

stories.title: A shared countdown timer is coming to Teams Rooms on Windows
stories.summary: Roadmap item 581893, in development: start, pause, resume or cancel a countdown timer from the room's touch console, with the countdown on the front-of-room display and in participants' meeting views. It needs a Teams Rooms Pro licence.
stories.for: Campus seminar and meeting rooms with Teams Rooms Pro

stories.title: Edge 158: switch workspaces in one window, and pin them with an emoji
stories.summary: Microsoft Edge 158 reached the Stable channel on 19 November. You can switch between workspaces inside your current window instead of opening one window each, pin the workspaces you use most and give each pinned one an emoji. A workspace per subject is one way to use it (our example).

stories.title: Edge 158's Remix lets you restyle supported pages
stories.summary: Remix in Edge 158 lets you personalise supported webpages with built-in appearance controls or plain-language requests. Changes stay in your own browser profile, with visible controls to pause or remove them, and organisations can turn it off with the RemixAvailability policy.
stories.for: Students and staff; school IT can manage it

stories.title: Programmed Training in Microsoft Foundry: you write the loop, Foundry runs the GPUs
stories.summary: In public preview, by request: a Python API (the Fine-Tuning Sessions SDK) where your code decides what to sample, how to score responses and when to update model weights, while Foundry runs the GPUs. It offers LoRA training for four open-weight models, billed by the tokens your loop processes.
stories.for: University AI labs and research students

stories.title: Foundry can now evaluate whole agent conversations
stories.summary: Multi-turn evaluation, in public preview in Microsoft Foundry, assesses complete agent conversations against your quality standards, not only single responses, because an answer can look right on its own inside a conversation that goes wrong. A student help agent is one thing to test this way (our example).
stories.for: University teams building agents for students and staff

stories.title: Exchange's High Volume Email will reach outside addresses too
stories.summary: Roadmap item 581778, in development: High Volume Email in Exchange Online, which today only sends inside your organisation, will also deliver bulk notifications, alerts and required messages to external recipients, but not marketing. Admins turn it on per HVE account, and billing is per external recipient.
stories.for: School IT (our example: required notices to families)

stories.title: A Cornell-LSU team wins a $200,000 Microsoft Quantum Pioneers prize
stories.summary: Cornell's Valla Fatemi and LSU's Constantin Schrade won a $200,000 prize in Microsoft's 2026 Quantum Pioneers Program, one of five winning submissions in its Hardware Track. The prize supports their work on faster ways, with a higher signal-to-noise ratio, to measure the parity of a qubit device.

stories.title: Microsoft's AI Transparency Initiative aims to make AI agents easier to audit
stories.summary: Announced at Ignite on 17 November, it has Microsoft working with more than 40 organisations, including Accenture, Adobe, KPMG, Mastercard and Volvo Cars, on open standards for AI transparency, security and governance across models and providers. It's at the standards stage, with a sign-up for organisations that want to help.
stories.for: University IT, security and compliance teams

stories.title: Teams' AI Interpreter for town halls and webinars is now due in February
stories.summary: Roadmap item 576711, in development: real-time, AI-powered audio interpretation for Teams town halls and webinars, with organisers choosing the supported languages. It's now listed for February 2027; when we covered it on 1 November it was due in December 2026. Open days and parent nights are two places it could help (our examples).
stories.for: Schools and universities running town halls and webinars

stories.title: Support for the Azure Functions OpenAI extension ends 20 April 2027
stories.summary: Microsoft will end support for the Azure Functions OpenAI extension on 20 April 2027. Apps that use it should move to the OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry or Azure AI Search SDKs directly, depending on the scenario, before then.
stories.for: Campus developers and student projects that use it

stories.title: Windows Insiders: full stereo on Bluetooth LE Audio earbuds, even with the mic on
stories.summary: In the Experimental channel, Bluetooth LE Audio devices can play full-range stereo while also using their microphone, for game chat, voice calls, voice typing and voice chat in Copilot Chat, on PCs that support Super Wideband Stereo with devices that support 48kHz playback.
stories.for: Students on calls and in game chat

stories.title: Windows Insiders get a People widget
stories.summary: Also in the Experimental channel: a People widget on the Widgets board (Windows key + W) brings together contacts from supported communication apps, so you can jump back into a conversation. Set up Phone Link, WhatsApp or both first.
stories.for: Students and staff on Windows Insider builds

stories.title: Polterguys: Possession Party is on Xbox Free Play Days
stories.summary: Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and Essential members can play Polterguys: Possession Party, a party game for up to 8 players who play ghosts possessing everyday objects, from 19 to 22 November. Deadlink and Slayers X are also in this round of Free Play Days.
stories.for: Students with Game Pass, after the bell

transcript.t: It's Sunday, and this is the Microsoft for Education Daily.
Here's your day in Microsoft updates, in 3 minutes flat.
On the same page: this week's best. Soon, Teams lets you pop out a sign language interpreter.
Their video stays in view while you share or switch layouts.
In class, Teams will let meeting organizers decide who can use Copilot and AI, due January.
Got Teams Rooms Pro? A shared countdown timer for the room is due in January.
Edge 158 is out: switch workspaces in one window, and pin them with an emoji.
Its new Remix lets you restyle supported pages w ith built-in controls or plain-language requests.
For university AI labs, Foundry's Programmed Training is in preview: your code, Foundry's GPUs.
Your Python decides what to sample, how to score it and when to update the weights.
Building a student help agent?
Foundry can now test whole conversations, not single answers, in preview.
School IT? Exchange's High Volume Email will also reach outside addresses, previewing in December.
A Cornell and LSU team won $200,000 from Microsoft's Quantum Pioneers Program.
And Microsoft's AI Transparency Initiative, with over 40 organisations, aims to make agents easier to audit.
The fine print?
Teams' live AI interpreter for webinars is now due February, not December.
And the Azure Functions OpenAI extension loses support next April, so plan your move.
After hours, Insiders get full stereo on Bluetooth LE Audio earbuds, even with the mic on.
There's a new People widget too, to jump back into chats from Phone Link or WhatsApp.
And this weekend, Game Pass members can try Polterguys, a ghostly party game for eight.
Shared timers, a visible interpreter, clear AI rules: everyone on the same page.
Zoom out, and it never stops shipping.
Some of it's shipped. The rest is on its way.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
You've been watching the Microsoft for Education Daily.
See you tomorrow.
